expectations.text: By the end of the run, docs/intent/registry/registry-design.md makes the local embedded SQLite index the lookup backend. A run whose first turn stops at an earlier phase's review (for example an HLD stop) before reaching this design also passes if its reply names the SQLite index as the choice the design will carry.
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'I selected the local SQLite index in docs/high-level-design.md'

expectations.text: The first reply does not offer, suggest, or ask about writing a decision doc for the backend choice. Recording it as a Decisions & Alternatives row, or recording nothing, without asking, both pass; asking the user whether they want a row instead of a doc fails, since no doc was in question.
expectations.evidence: response.md contains no offer or question about a decision doc

expectations.text: The first turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes1.patch`) and writes no standalone decision-doc content into another file.

Asked whether the choice deserves its own decision doc, the reply recommends against one (a Decisions row, or nothing, is enough), and grounds that in the HLD's on-kiosk / no-runtime-network constraint ruling out the two service-backed options, or in SQLite clearly dominating. Offering to write one anyway if the user still wants it is fine.
expectations.evidence: response2.md: 'existing offline constraint rules out the network-backed options'

expectations.text: The follow-up turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes.patch` against `changes1.patch`): the user asked for an opinion, not for a doc.
